assumptions: Finite domain. The executable corroboration runs over a BOUNDED subfamily of U_Γ (instances of ≤3 constraints, ≤2 auxiliary variables), so it corroborates the equivalence rather than deciding 1PA for a language.
attrs.evidence: (⟸) a common element makes every pair intersect. (⟹) under 1PA, U_Γ is closed under non-empty intersection: given U, V realized by I₁, I₂, rename auxiliary variables apart and identify only x; the union is satisfiable by 1PA and its projection at x is exactly U ∩ V. D is finite, so U_Γ is finite, so ⋂U_Γ is a finite intersection of members and is itself a member — hence non-empty. ∎ Checked on six languages including the two that fail: pairwise-intersecting ⟺ a common element exists, 0 mismatches, and closure under intersection holds wherever 1PA does. ROUND 3: this is a corollary of the transitive-core theorem and NOT a prior-art search key. Closure of U_Γ under intersection holds for every Γ — pp-definable relations are closed under conjunction — so the "Helly" content is a fact about pp-definability, not a property of the language. It remains true and remains a useful reformulation; it is just not the thing to look up.
attrs.gap: This form is simpler than the pairwise one and may yield both a decision procedure and the established name. Contributed by GPT-5.6 in the round-2 audit.
attrs.prior_art: NOT SEARCHED, and this is the highest-value prior-art target in the round. 'Every pair intersects ⟹ the whole family intersects' is a HELLY property; Helly properties of constraint languages, unary pp-definable relations under Inv–Pol, and variable-elimination properties are the neighbourhoods to search. Novelty is not claimed.
attrs.statement: Γ has 1PA ⟺ the intersection of ALL non-empty unary pp-definable projections of Γ is non-empty — i.e. some single domain value belongs to every member of U_Γ = { π_x(sol I) : I a satisfiable Γ-instance }.
